Package dev.relism.flash.ext.security.oauthserver

Class OAuthServer

java.lang.Object
dev.relism.flash.ext.security.oauthserver.OAuthServer
All Implemented Interfaces:
Bound, AuthenticationMechanism, Module
public final class OAuthServer extends Object implements Module, AuthenticationMechanism, Bound
An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the application's own users and resources. A user signs in the way the application's security chain signs anyone in, consents on the application's page, and the client receives an RFC 9068 access token for one of the application's resources — which this module, as an AuthenticationMechanism, then authenticates. 

 app.install(new SecurityModule().origin("https://app.example").loginPage("/login"),
             new OAuthServer("/mcp").store(store).signingKeys(keys));

Authorization code with PKCE S256 (the only grant a user takes part in), refresh tokens that rotate and revoke their family on reuse, client_credentials for clients the application registers itself; RFC 8414 metadata, RFC 7591 registration, client ID metadata documents, RFC 8707 resource indicators, RFC 7009 revocation, RFC 9207 iss in the authorization response. The issuer is the application's Security.origin(Request). Needs a CacheManager in the app, for client metadata documents and discovery.

    • store

    • signingKeys

      public OAuthServer signingKeys(String jwkSet)
      The signing keys, as a JWK set whose first key is a private P-256 key — see generateSigningKeys(). Unset, a key is generated at boot, and every token dies with the process.

    • subjects

      public OAuthServer subjects(Function<SecurityIdentity,OAuthSubject> subjects)
      Whom an authorization names, and what its tokens carry — and who may authorize at all: throw to refuse a caller. A credential narrower than its user, like an API key, must not become a token with all the user's rights. Default: the principal's name, no claims, anyone signed in.

    • scopes

      public OAuthServer scopes(String... scopes)
      The scopes a client may be granted; any other it asks for is left out of the grant. Default: none.

    • accessTokenLifetime

    • consentPage

      public OAuthServer consentPage(String consentPage)
      The application's page asking a signed-in user to allow a client, sent the authorization request as its query string. It reads GET /oauth/authorize/request with that same query, and posts it back to /oauth/authorize with consent=allow or consent=deny. Default /consent.

    • registration

      public OAuthServer registration(boolean open)
      Whether any client may register itself at REGISTER (RFC 7591). Default true.

      public Principal authenticate(Request req)
